rationale.usefulness: The actual Core and CLI documentation provide a useful shared reference for React developers and coding agents: component discovery, templates, version metadata, themes and source ownership. The report translates these into reviewable exercise, draft-queue, research-library and shot-review pilots without inventing media-generation features. React 19 and package/version caveats make adoption work explicit.
rationale.impact: Queryable design-system knowledge can meaningfully improve agent-assisted frontend implementation and reduce invented component APIs. This is a focused tooling contribution, not a demonstrated general model advance; internal adoption scale is a publisher claim and there is no comparative productivity or accessibility study.
rationale.novelty: The coherent machine-readable manifest, typed responses, multi-domain search, project-version delegation and human/agent common reference are a distinctive packaging of design-system knowledge. Components, CSS-variable themes and source ejection are established techniques, so the evidence supports meaningful differentiation rather than exceptional novelty.
rationale.maturity: Detailed setup and diagnostics documentation, public implementation and an established internal lineage support a usable public offering. The current beta label, unpublished Lab, canary-only chart packages, differing inventory counts and absence of an executed build or accessibility audit prevent a higher readiness rating. The report correctly treats doctor warnings and integration findings at their stated scope.
rationale.openness: The actual MIT license permits modification, redistribution and sale with notice retention, while public source, exported internals and swizzle support inspection and local ownership. A 9 reflects strong software openness; third-party dependency and asset rights remain separate, and complete reproducibility across every documented setup was not tested.
